title: Cross-surface LTS support grid and staged upgrade choreography
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a single authoritative LTS support grid and rollout choreography that defines compatibility guarantees and upgrade tooling for all inference surfaces (serving runtime, Redwood API, official SDKs, and Redwood Console). Deliverables: 1) A machine-readable support matrix mapping LTS channels to supported patch/feature semantics per-surface, 2) A staged rollout playbook (canary cohorts, gating checks, rollback triggers) that CI/CD and on-prem upgrade tooling can consume, 3) Preflight validation tooling and compatibility test harness for automated pre-release checks, 4) Migration/compatibility notes and CLI helpers for runtime KV/cache state and SDK/API contract migrations. Background: Current LTS conversations are fragmented across runtime, API, SDK and Console teams. We need one coherent spec that: - Clearly states what backwards/forwards compatibility we guarantee between LTS and minor releases (e.g., runtime ABI for model execution, API request/response fields, SDK client method signatures, console dashboard schema), - Enumerates supported upgrade paths (e.g., runtime 1.9 -> runtime 2.0 LTS coexistence window, console client compatibility window), - Defines what classes of fixes are safe in LTS (security/critical bugfix only vs. allowed behavioral deltas). Key design decisions to capture: - Runtime: LTS will guarantee KV cache serialization compatibility across patch releases within the same major; cross-major will require KV invalidation or migration procedures. We must document exact schema versioning and provide a migration tool. - API: Stable endpoints (text/generate, embeddings) will be guaranteed request/response stable for X patch releases; new optional fields allowed but must be additive and non-breaking. Deprecation will use a two-cycle notice. - SDKs: Adopt semantic compatibility windows: SDK pinned to runtime/API major with a supported patch skew (e.g., SDK v2.* is supported against API runtime 2.x with +/-1 minor). Provide a compatibility matrix file consumed by the CI. - Console: UI and backend schema compatibility guaranteed for dashboard read-only operations during rollouts; write operations that rely on new API fields will be gated. Rollout choreography (summary): 1) Preflight: run compatibility test matrix against staging fleet and sample customer datasets (automated). 2) Canary stage: release to 1% of traffic (and one internal customer cohort) for 24h; metrics evaluated. 3) Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated health gates and manual approval at 25%. 4) Fallback: instant rollback on threshold breaches or manual abort. Health gates and triggers: - Latency increase > 20% over baseline for 5m -> fail canary - Error rate > 0.5% absolute increase -> fail - Quality regression on evaluation prompts (pre-defined prompt set): any top-level regression triggers manual hold - Resource regression (GPU memory, kernel failures) -> automatic rollback Automation & tooling: - preflight-validator CLI (runs API conformance, runtime KV roundtrip, SDK smoke tests) - upgrade-runner (orchestrates staged rollout, integrates with console for approvals) - compatibility-matrix JSON artifact stored with release that contains per-surface guarantees and known incompatibilities Acceptance criteria: - Support matrix doc + JSON artifact produced and reviewed by runtime/API/SDK/Console leads - preflight-validator prototype that runs full matrix in CI within 45 minutes - rollout playbook with measurable gates and default cohort percentages checked into runbooks repo - migration scripts for KV cache serialization or documented invalidation path - E2E smoke test demonstrating rollback behavior in canary stage Risks & trade-offs recorded: - Stricter guarantees reduce developer velocity (fewer behavioral fixes in LTS) but improve customer predictability. We'll recommend a pragmatic policy: only security and regression fixes in LTS, feature/backcompat changes via minor channels with clear migration docs. - Time to build migration tooling vs. forcing cache invalidation: initial release prefers documented invalidation with tooling sprint in parallel. Implementation plan (high-level): Week 1: Draft matrix and circulate to surface leads; Week 2: Build preflight-validator scaffold + CI integration; Week 3: Implement compatibility JSON artifact generation and add to release pipeline; Week 4: Author rollout playbook and runbooks, run staged rehearsals. Links & artifacts: - RFC: https://drive.redwood/example-lts-matrix-rfc (placeholder) - Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-infra/pull/456 - Design notes: https://confluence.redwood/lts-cross-surface (placeholder)
acceptance_criteria: Authoritative LTS support matrix published as JSON and human readable doc
preflight-validator runs full compatibility matrix in CI under 45m
Rollout playbook committed with default gates and cohort sizes
Compatibility artifact is attached to every release and consumed by SDK CI
Migration instructions or tooling available for runtime KV/cache schema changes
